headline: New algorithms advance viral alignment, RNA structure, protein comparison, and k-mer sets
label: Alignment And Comparison Algorithms
summary: Four May 2026 preprints present alignment and comparison methods for viral genomes, RNA structures, protein structures, and k-mer spectra.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the redesign of comparison primitives so that biological structure is represented explicitly in the computation. Min-Frame Transformation re-encodes nucleotides over a transformed alphabet so that MUM seeding yields longer, more contiguous matches for viral genome alignment. CoSTAR performs exact search over stem-level partial maps under topological constraints to align pseudoknotted RNA structures, benchmarked on 2100 Rfam pairwise comparisons. Ordered Gromov-Hausdorff incorporates residue order into protein structure comparison via a fast surrogate algorithm. Fast Set Operations provides intersection, union, and difference on SBWT-encoded k-mer spectra alongside a memory-efficient SBWT construction algorithm. What is new across these preprints is that ordering, topology, or set structure is built into each method's core search or metric, with computational efficiency addressed in the same design.
